185401 := Type of Feat: Metamagic
Prerequisite: Quicken Spell, Arcane Scholar of Candlekeep level 10.
Specifics: Quickened spells occupy spell slots three levels higher than normal (instead of four levels higher).
Quickened spells can be cast instantaneously, making them invulnerable to interruption. A quickened spell is cast as a free action, and another action can be attempted within the same round, including the casting of another spell. Only one quickened spell can be cast per round.
Use: A (improved) quickened spell occupies a spell slot three levels higher than normal. Saving throws and opposed rolls, such as those made when <i>dispel magic</i> is cast, are not affected.

185532 := <color=Gold><b>Red Wizard</b></color>

<color=Red>(PRESTIGE CLASS: This class is not available at character creation and must be unlocked by meeting special requirements, listed below.)</color>

The Red Wizards are the masters of Thay. They focus on a school of magic more intently than any specialist, achieving incredible mastery of magic within a very narrow focus.

<color=Gold>Requirements:</color>

<b>Race:</b> Human

<b>Alignment:</b> Any nongood.

<b>Skills:</b> Spellcraft 8 ranks.

<b>Feats:</b> One metamagic or item creation feat (other than Scribe Scroll), Spell Penetration, Greater Spell Penetration.

<b>Spellcasting:</b> Must be a specialist wizard and able to cast 3rd-level arcane spells.

<color=Gold>Class Features:</color>

- <b>Hit Die:</b> d4

- <b>Base Attack Bonus:</b> Low.

- <b>High Saves:</b> Will

- <b>Weapon Proficiencies:</b> Red Wizards gain no weapon proficiencies.

- <b>Armor Proficiencies:</b> Red Wizards gain no armor proficiencies.

- <b>Skill Points:</b> 2 + Int Modifier.

- <b>Class Skills:</b> Bluff, Concentration, Craft Alchemy, Intimidate, Lore, and Spellcraft.

- <b>Spells per Day/Spells Known:</b> When a new Red Wizard level is gained, the character gains new spells per day (and spells known, if applicable) as though he had gained a level in wizard. Red Wizard arcane spell progression cannot be applied to other classes, such as sorcerers or bards.

- <b>Enhanced Specialization:</b> Upon becoming a Red Wizard, the character becomes even more skilled at casting spells from his chosen school of specialization. The Difficulty Check for saves against spells cast from the specialist school is increased by +1, and the Red Wizard receives +1 to his caster level when attempting to penetrate spell resistance when casting a spell from the specialist school.

- <b>Specialist Defense:</b> A Red Wizard gains a bonus on saving throws against spells from his specialist school. This bonus is +1 at 1st level, +2 at 3rd level, +3 at 7th level, and +4 at 9th level.

- <b>Spell Power:</b> At 2nd level, the Red Wizard's effective caster level for determining level-dependent variable checks is increased by +1. This bonus increases by +1 at every even Red Wizard level (+2 at 4th level, +3 at 6th level, +4 at 8th level, and +5 at 10th level).

- <b>Wizard Bonus Feat:</b> At 5th level, the Red Wizard gains a bonus metamagic or item creation feat. The Red Wizard gains an additional metamagic or item creation feat at 10th level.

185803 := <color=Gold><b>Half-Drow</b></color>

Half-drow are often just as dark-hearted as their elven parents, but with a bitter resentment that comes from knowing that they are considered second-class members of drow society. Despite this, good half-drow are much less rare than good drow. Half-drow have dusky skin, silver or white hair, and a broad range of eye colors.

<color=Gold><b>Racial Traits:</b></color>

- <b>Hardiness vs. Enchantments:</b> Immunity to magical sleep effects, +2 racial bonus to saving throws against enchantment spells or effects.

- <b>Darkvision:</b> Half-drow can see in the dark up to 60 feet.

- <b>Keen Senses:</b> +1 racial bonus to Listen, Search, and Spot checks.

- <b>Amiable:</b> +2 racial bonus to Diplomacy and Bluff checks.

- <b>Favored Class:</b> Any. When determining whether a multiclass half-drow takes an experience point penalty, her highest-level class does not count.

185911 := Spirit Shaman
185912 := Spirit Shamans
185913 := spirit shaman
185914 := <color=Gold><b>Spirit Shaman</b></color>

Master of the spirit world, the spirit shaman follows a different divine tradition than the cleric or druid. Her world is filled with powerful, living spirits, some helpful and some malign. By bargaining with these spirits, the spirit shaman gains power over the natural world and mighty divine magic with which to aid her comrades or smite her enemies. Creatures which are considered spirits include fey, elementals, and incorporeal undead such as wraiths and shadows.

<color=Gold>Class Features:</color>

- <b>Hit Die:</b> d8

- <b>Base Attack Bonus:</b> Medium.

- <b>High Saves:</b> Fortitude and Will.

- <b>Weapon Proficiencies:</b> Club, dagger, dart, handaxe, spear, quarterstaff, sling, shortbow, throwing axe, and light crossbow.

- <b>Armor Proficiencies:</b>  Light armor and shields (except tower shields).

- <b>Skill Points:</b> 4 + Int modifier per level,  x4 at first level.

- <b>Class Skills:</b> Concentration, Craft Alchemy, Diplomacy, Heal, Lore, Listen, Spellcraft, Spot, and Survival

- <b>Spells:</b> A spirit shaman casts divine spells, which are drawn from the druid spell list. Unlike the druid, a spirit shaman does not have to memorize his spells in advance, but he is only able to learn a limited number of spells. To cast a spell, a spirit shaman must have a Wisdom score equal to at least 10 + the spell level (Wis 10 for 0-level spells, Wis 11 for 1st-level spells, and so forth). A spirit shaman's Charisma determines the Difficulty Check of his spells.

- <b>Spirit Guide:</b> Spirit shamans have a spirit guide, a personification of the spirit world, which exists only inside her mind and soul. The spirit guide grants the spirit shaman the Alertness feat at 1st level.

- <b>Chastise Spirits:</b> Beginning at 2nd level, a spirit shaman can deal 1d4 damage/shaman level to all spirits within 30 feet of herself. The affected spirits get a Will save (DC 10 + spirit shaman level + Charisma modifier) for half damage. This ability can be used a number of times per day equal to 3 + the shaman's Charisma modifier.

- <b>Detect Spirits:</b> At 3rd level, the spirit shaman gains the ability to use her spirit guide to detect any nearby spirits. Detected spirits will appear on the minimap. This effect lasts for 10 minutes.

- <b>Blessing of the Spirits:</b> At 4th level, the spirit shaman gains a +2 deflection bonus to AC and a +2 resistance bonus on saves against attacks and effects made by spirits. This effect may be dispelled, but the spirit shaman can reactivate it at will.

- <b>Follow the Guide:</b> A spirit shaman's spirit guide helps her maintain control of her mind.  At 5th level, if a spirit shaman is affected by a mind-affecting spell or effect and fails her saving throw, she can attempt it again immediately at the same DC. She only gets this one extra chance to succeed on her saving throw. This ability does not stack with similar abilities granted by other classes the spirit shaman may have.

- <b>Ghost Warrior:</b> At 6th level, the spirit shaman is able to strike spirits with unerring accuracy. The spirit shaman ignores all concealment and miss chance effects when fighting against spirits.

- <b>Warding of the Spirits:</b> At 7th level, the spirit shaman is able to grant his party members a +2 deflection bonus to AC and a +2 resistance bonus on saves against attacks and effects made by spirits. This ability is usable once per day and lasts for 10 minutes per shaman level. The effects from this ability do not stack with the spirit shaman's Blessing of the Spirits effect.

- <b>Spirit Form:</b> At 9th level, the spirit shaman gains the ability to become temporarily incorporeal once per day, gaining a 50% concealment bonus for 5 rounds. The spirit shaman can use this ability twice per day at 15th level, and three times per day at 20th level.

- <b>Recall Spirit:</b> At 11th level, the spirit shaman gains the ability to restore life to the recently deceased once per day. This effect is similar to the <i>raise dead</i> spell.

- <b>Weaken Spirits:</b> At 16th level, the spirit shaman can choose to strip all spirits within 30 feet of herself of their defensive abilities by expending a daily use of her Chastise Spirits ability. When a spirit is weakened, it loses its spell resistance, any damage reduction, and any miss chance or concealment effect it may have. This weakening effect lasts for 1 round plus 1 additional round for every 3 spirit shaman levels. Spirits that make their Will save (DC 10 + spirit shaman level + Charisma modifier) are unaffected by the weakening effect.

- <b>Spirit Journey:</b> At 17th level, the spirit shaman gains the ability to vanish bodily into the spirit world once per day. This effect lasts for 1 round per spirit shaman level, and during this time the spirit shaman cannot attack or be attacked.

- <b>Favored of the Spirits:</b> At 19th level, the spirit shaman can perform a special rite to guard herself from death. Under this protection, the spirit shaman instantly heals 10 hit points per spirit shaman level, up to 150 hit points, if she is reduced to 0 hit points. Once the rite's protection has been discharged, the spirit shaman must rest to regain the favor of the spirits.

- <b> Spirit Who Walks:</b> At 20th level, the spirit shaman becomes one with the spirit world. She gains damage reduction 5/cold iron, a +3 resistance bonus to saves against enchantments, and the Low-light Vision feat if she doesn't already have it.

186045 := <color=Gold><b>Stormlord</b></color>

<color=Red>(PRESTIGE CLASS: This class is not available at character creation and must be unlocked by meeting special requirements, listed below.)</color>

Stormlords wield thunder and lightning like a warrior wields his sword. Because of their command of one of the most destructive aspects of nature, stormlords are viewed with awe and fear by lesser folk, regardless of their motivation.

<color=Gold>Requirements:</color>

<b>Base Save Bonus:</b> Fortitude +4

<b>Feats:</b> Toughness, Great Fortitude, and Weapon Focus (Spear, Throwing Axe, Dart, or Shuriken).

<b>Spellcasting:</b> Able to cast 3rd-level divine spells.

<color=Gold>Class Features:</color>

- <b>Hit Die:</b> d8

- <b>Base Attack Bonus:</b> Medium.

- <b>High Saves:</b> Fortitude and Will.

- <b>Weapon Proficiencies:</b> Stormlords gain no weapon proficiencies.

- <b>Armor Proficiencies:</b> Stormlords gain no armor proficiencies.

- <b>Skill Points:</b> 2 + Int Modifier.

- <b>Class Skills:</b> Concentration, Diplomacy, Intimidate, Lore, Survival.

- <b>Spells per Day/Spells Known:</b> When a new stormlord level is gained, the character gains new spells per day (and spells known, if applicable) as though he had gained a level in whatever divine spellcasting class gave him access to 3rd-level divine spells. If the character has more than one applicable divine spellcasting class, he must pick one to improve.

- <b>Electricity Resistance:</b> At 1st level, a stormlord gains electrical resistance 5. This increases to electrical resistance 10 at 4th level and electrical resistance 15 at 7th level.

- <b>Enhanced Stormlord Weapons:</b> At 1st level, the stormlord's thrown weapons and spears count as +1 weapons. This bonus increases to +2 at 6th level and +3 at 9th level.

- <b>Shock Weapon:</b> At 2nd level, a stormlord may enchant any equipped thrown weapon or spear to deal an additional 1d8 points of electricity damage.  This effect lasts 20 rounds.

- <b>Shocking Burst Weapon:</b> At 5th level, a stormlord may enchant any equipped thrown weapon or spear to deal an additional 1d8 points of electricity damage and an extra 2d8 points of weapon damage on a critical hit (4d8 if the critical multiplier is x3, 6d8 if the critical multiplier is x4).  This effect lasts 20 rounds.

- <b>Shocking Burst and Sonic Weapon:</b> At 8th level, the stormlord may enchant any equipped thrown weapon or spear to deal an additional 1d8 points of electrical damage, an extra 1d8 points of sonic damage, and an extra 2d8 points of weapon damage on a critical hit (4d8 if the critical multiplier is x3, 6d8 if the critical multiplier is x4). This effect lasts 20 rounds.

- <b>Electricity Immunity:</b> At 9th level, the stormlord gains immunity to electrical damage.

- <b>Extended Storm Avatar:</b> At 10th level, the stormlord can cast <i>storm avatar</i> as if he were a druid with a caster level equal to his character level. This ability is usable once per day and otherwise functions as the 8th-level druid spell of the same name, lasting twice the normal duration.

186146 := <color=Gold><b>Invisible Blade</b></color>

<color=Red>(PRESTIGE CLASS: This class is not available at character creation and must be unlocked by meeting special requirements, listed below.)</color>

Invisible blades are deadly fighters who prefer to use daggers and related weapons in combat. Their training and techniques with these weapons make them just as lethal as any well-armed fighter. Invisible blades enjoy cultivating misconceptions about the level of danger they present, and they relish any chance to demonstrate that the most unimposing weapons can be the most lethal.

<color=Gold>Requirements:</color>

<b>Skills:</b> Bluff 8 ranks.

<b>Feats:</b> Feint, Two-Weapon Fighting, Weapon Focus (Dagger or Kukri).

<color=Gold>Class Features:</color>

- <b>Hit Die:</b> d6

- <b>Base Attack Bonus:</b> High.

- <b>High Saves:</b> Reflex.

- <b>Weapon Proficiencies:</b> Invisible blades gain no weapon proficiencies.

- <b>Armor Proficiencies:</b> Invisible blades gain no armor proficiencies.

- <b>Skill Points:</b> 4 + Int Modifier.

- <b>Class Skills:</b> Bluff, Craft Alchemy, Craft Armor, Craft Weapon, Craft Trap, Hide, Listen, Move Silently, Parry, Perform, Spot, and Tumble.

- <b>Bleeding Wound:</b> At 1st level, when an invisible blade hits with a successful sneak attack, he inflicts a bleeding wound that deals 2 points of damage per round for 3 rounds. This damage stacks with previous damage caused by a Bleeding Wound attack. He must be either unarmed or wielding only light weapons in order to inflict a Bleeding Wound. At 3rd level, the damage increases to 4 points per round, and at 5th level, it increases to 6 points per round. Each level of Bleeding Wound counts as one die of sneak attack damage for purposes of class and feat prerequisites.

- <b>Unfettered Defense:</b> An invisible blade benefits from an increased survival instinct during combat. Because of this sixth sense, he adds 1 point of his Intelligence bonus (if any) per invisible blade level to his Armor Class in addition to any other modifiers he would normally receive. If the invisible blade is caught flat-footed or is otherwise denied his Dexterity modifier to Armor Class, he also loses this bonus. Unfettered Defense functions only when an invisible blade is not wearing armor and is not wielding a ranged weapon.

- <b>Feint Mastery:</b> At 5th level, an invisible blade armed with a light weapon becomes so sure of his ability to mislead opponents that he cannot roll less than 5 on his Bluff check when using the Feint feat.

- <b>Air Resistance:</b> Air genasi have electricity resistance 5.

- <b> Favored Class:</b> Fighter. An air genasi's fighter class does not count when determining whether he takes an experience point penalty for multiclassing.

- <b>Level Adjustment +1:</b> Air genasi are slightly more powerful and gain levels more slowly than other races. It will take more experience for an air genasi to reach level 2 than it would for normal races, for example.

Brilliant Air Essences are also suitable for enchanting. To enchant an item, place it in the Enchanter's Satchel along with one or more Brilliant Air Essences, then cast the appropriate spell on the item. Use up to four Brilliant Air Essences for more powerful enchantments. Any item can hold up to three enchantments total, or four if the enchanter is of epic level. The required caster level depends upon the number of essences you are using:

1 Brilliant Essence -- Caster Level 12
2 Brilliant Essences -- Caster Level 15
3 Brilliant Essences -- Caster Level 18
4 Brilliant Essences -- Caster Level 21

Standard recipes are:

Craft Magic Arms and Armor
<i>Weapons</i>: Shock Weapon. Spell: Call Lightning or Lightning Bolt
<i>Armor</i>: Weight Reduction. Spell: Protection from Energy

Craft Wondrous Item
<i>Cloak</i>: Energy Resistance (electricity) and Save Bonus versus electrical attacks. Spell: Endure Elements
<i>Gloves</i>: Unarmed Damage Bonus (electricity). Spell: Shocking Grasp
<i>Amulet</i>: Energy Resistance (electricity). Spell: Resist Energy
<i>Rings</i>: Save Bonus versus electricity attacks. Spell: Resistance

*Note that while the Cloak provides two benefits, the amulet and ring bonuses are greater for a given number of essences.

195693 := Favored Soul
195694 := Favored Souls
195695 := favored soul
195696 := <color=Gold><b>Favored Soul</b></color>

The favored soul follows the path of the cleric but is able to channel divine power with surprising ease. She is able to perform the same tasks as her fellow divine spellcasters but with virtually no study. Favored souls cast their spells naturally, as much through force of personality as through study. Though this gives them extraordinary divine abilities no normal person could ever match, they see their gift as a call to action, and so in some ways may lag behind their more studious colleagues.

<color=Gold>Class Features:</color>

- <b>Hit Die:</b> d8

- <b>Base Attack Bonus:</b> Medium.

- <b>High Saves:</b> All.

- <b>Weapon Proficiencies:</b> Simple weapons and deity's favored weapon.

- <b>Armor Proficiencies:</b>  Light armor, medium armor, and shields (except tower shields).

- <b>Skill Points:</b> 2 + Int modifier per level, x4 at first level.

- <b>Class Skills:</b> Concentration, Craft Alchemy, Craft Armor, Craft Weapon, Diplomacy, Heal, Lore, Parry, and Spellcraft.

- <b>Spells:</b> A favored soul casts divine spells which are drawn from the cleric spell list. She can cast any spell she knows without preparing it ahead of time the way a cleric must. To cast a spell, a favored soul must have a Charisma score of 10 + the spell's level (Cha 10 for 0-level spells, Cha 11 for 1st-level spells, and so forth). The Difficulty Class for  a saving throw against a favored soul's spell is 10 + the spell's level + the favored soul's Wisdom modifier. Unlike a cleric, a favored soul's selection of spells is limited, but at 4th level, and at every even-numbered favored soul level after that, the favored soul may swap a spell she already knows for another spell of the same level. In effect, the favored soul "loses" the old spell in exchange for the new one.

- <b>Deity's Weapon Proficiency:</b> Favored souls gain a weapon proficiency feat that allows them to use their deity's favored weapon. (For example, favored souls of Kelemvor will gain the Exotic Weapon Proficiency feat, enabling them to use a bastard sword.)

- <b>Deity's Weapon Focus:</b> At 3rd level, a favored soul gains the Weapon Focus feat with her deity's favored weapon.

- <b>Energy Resistance:</b> At 5th level, a favored soul chooses an energy type and gains resistance 10 against that type. At 10th level and 15th level, the character gains resistance 10 against another energy type of her choosing.

- <b>Deity's Weapon Specialization:</b> At 12th level, a favored soul gains the Weapon Specialization feat with her deity's favored weapon.

- <b>Haste:</b> At 17th level, a favored soul gains the ability to cast <i>haste</i> three times per day.

- <b>Damage Reduction:</b> At 20th level, a favored soul gains damage reduction. She may choose between damage reduction 10/silver or damage reduction 10/cold iron.

195891 := hagspawn
195892 := <color=Gold><b>Hagspawn</b></color>

Sons of malicious, predatory mothers, hagspawn are not a complete race, as there are no females of their kind. Hags continue their awful lineage by taking human males for mates, usually murdering and devouring the hapless captive later. The female children of a hag quickly grow into hags like their mothers, but the male children are hagspawn - half-human outcasts. Feared and hated by normal humans, hagspawn must make their way in the world by dint of their strength, hardiness, and sheer determination.

<color=Gold><b>Racial Traits:</b></color>

- <b>Ability Adjustments:</b> +2 Strength, +2 Constitution, -2 Charisma.

- <b>Darkvision:</b> Hagspawn can see in the dark up to 60 feet.

- <b>Natural Armor:</b> +2 natural armor bonus.

- <b>Spell Resistant:</b> Spell resistance of 11 + character level.

- <b>Favored Class:</b> Barbarian. A multiclass hagspawn's barbarian class does not count when determining whether he takes an experience point penalty.

- <b>Level Adjustment +2:</b> Hagspawn are more powerful and gain levels more slowly than other races. It will take more experience for a hagspawn to reach level 2 than it would for normal races, for example.

199435 := Periapt of the Lost Witch
199436 := Arduelth, a young witch, had spent her life living under the shadow of Thay, and wished to study for a magical means to empower Rashemen, so she left on a <i>dajemma</i> - the customary Rashemi journey of self-discovery. Years later she returned, a haunted look in her eyes. Around her neck she wore an amulet that glowed with power - only the first of the artifacts she claimed to have learned how to create. She spoke long and passionately of how they could make use of such items - to not only bring peace to Rashemen, but break the back of Thay. The hathrans narrowed their eyes behind their masks as she spoke, fearing the young woman's intensity: but they listened, and gravely made her one of them.

Before long, the witches began to regret their decision. The young woman seemed obsessed with the idea of creating more items of greater and more sinister properties... and her plans grew more and more elaborate, from freeing the slaves of Thay to enslaving the Red Wizards in their place, sapping them of their power for her own devices. It was suspected that Arduelth had become a durthan, eternal enemy of the hathrans - but another witch saw once that she communed with something far darker. Though the young woman still dreamed of peace and freedom for her people, she had given herself over to a dark entity - her pure intentions savaged by the lengths she would dare go to achieve them.

Though it seems Arduelth's life has come to an end, the amulet still glows with a same promising light... as if it carried a fraction of its former wearer's soul, and the determination to see her plans come to fruition - whatever the cost.

201061 := You have lost control of the hunger for spirits that has recently manifested inside of you. Your body now requires a periodic influx of energy obtained through the consumption of spirits, or it will eventually wither and die.

The vertical green bar represents your present level of spirit energy. It will drop over time (except during conversation), and as it falls, you will weaken at an accelerating rate. Each of the watermarks on the bar denotes a point at which your curse worsens to a new stage of debilitation. There are six stages of this affliction, the final of which is death. You may mouse over the watermark icons at any time to see what effects a particular stage of the affliction carries.
201063 := Several new abilities are available to you (via the feats tab of your character sheet) that will provide a means to replenish your spirit energy:

Devour Spirit can be cast on spirits (elementals, fey, and incorporeal undead). It yields a fixed amount of spirit energy, plus a bonus if it kills the target. Killing blows will also grant you a spirit essence, which can be used in crafting. Targets who are "Near Death" will die when devoured.

Suppress can be cast instead of Devour Spirit. It typically generates less spirit energy, but it does not require the consumption of a spirit. Its effectiveness increases if spirits are nearby.  
201064 := The horizontal bar below the spirit energy bar is a measurement of your craving for spirits. The more you crave spirits, the faster your spirit energy is used up. 

Giving in to your urge to devour spirits more than once per day will tend to make you crave them more, while actively fighting to gain control over your hunger through the Suppress ability will ease that craving. Use extreme caution when deciding whether to devour spirits if you have already done so once that day - what may seem like a safe move to keep your health high could quite quickly lead you down a slippery slope where you are in constant need of spirits to devour just to stay alive.

You may minimize your spirit-energy bar at any time by clicking the button at its upper right corner. All of the key details will still be made visible to you in this mode.

207008 := This small bag can be used to enchant items and functions like a portable workbench.

To enchant an item, simply place it in this satchel along with one or more brilliant <i>essences</i>, then cast the appropriate spell as indicated in the essence's description. For example, to create a frost weapon, place one brilliant water essence and any weapon into the Enchanter's Satchel, then cast <i>ice storm</i> on the satchel.

Essences are automatically distilled from the remains of many creatures, such as elementals and most beasts. Such essences are typically only of volatile quality and ten must be combined using a Shaper's Alembic to create a brilliant variety.

Rarer recipes and essences might be discovered throughout your adventures.
207009 := This powerful alembic allows you to convert, combine, and divide essences. Essences are used to enchant items. They are automatically distilled from the remains of many creatures, such as elementals and most beasts. Typically, only volatile essences are found and the alembic must be used to convert them into brilliant essences for enchanting purposes. Items are enchanted by placing them in the Enchanter's Satchel along with one or more essences, and then casting the appropriate spell. Many standard recipes are explained in the item description for any brilliant essence.

The abilities of the Shaper's Alembic include:
1. Combine Essences. Using this ability on a stack of lesser essences converts them into a more powerful one. No value is lost.
2. Divide Essence. Using this ability on a powerful essence converts it into an equivalent number of lesser essences. No value is lost.
3. Convert Essence. When used on a stack of elemental essences (fire, air, earth, water), two are converted into a single power essence of the same quality. When used on a power essence, several lesser essences are created of each elemental type.

It has since acquired several owners over the ages, and was most recently used to defeat the King of Shadows. Now fully reforged, the power of this ancient artifact has finally been restored.

Designed to utilize its power intelligently, the sword adapts to its wielder, giving powers it deems appropriate for its master's abilities.
With every strike, the sword has a 20% chance of dealing bonus cold damage and a 20% chance of emitting a sonic wave, similar to the spell, Sound Burst. The sword has been further enchanted with numerous abilities, each quite potent in its own right:

<b>Spell-Like Abilities</b>:

These abilities consume the sword's charges. They may be replenished by casting spells on the blade, which will absorb the energies. Alternately, the sword has been designed to recharge itself in battle, slowly restoring its power with every successful attack.

<b>Chilling Wrath</b>: Three beams of freezing cold energy are directed at a single target as separate ranged touch attacks. <b>Infinite Resonance</b>: A massive sound wave is sent radiating away from the wielder in a circular radius, dealing large amounts of damage and deafening and knocking down enemies unable to resist its power (Fortitude save prevents).

<b>Unity of Will</b>: All creatures in view of the sword are affected by its power. Allies to the wielder, united in purpose, are granted bonuses similar to those found in the spells, Mind Blank and Heroism. Nearby enemies are given penalties similar to the spells Fear and Crushing Despair (Will save negates).

<b>Unbroken Circle</b>: The wielder is protected from physical harm and magical attacks in a manner similar to the spells, Premonition and Spell Mantle.

<b>Perfect Rejuvenation</b>: The wielder is restored as if affected by the spells, Greater Restoration and Regenerate.

<b>Sword Forms</b>:

The sword bearer may magically alter the edge of the blade to produce different effects, several times per day:

<b>Penetrating Edge</b>: For a short while, all physical damage done is maximized.

<b>Anti-Magic Edge</b>: For a short while, every time the wielder lands a blow with the sword, the target must save or be affected by Mordenkainen's Disjunction.

<b>Defensive Edge</b>: For a short while, the sword confers a significant bonus to the wielder's armor class.

207374 := This small bag can be used to enchant items and functions like a portable workbench.

To enchant an item, simply place it in this satchel along with one or more brilliant <i>essences</i>, then cast the appropriate spell as indicated in the essence's description. For example, to create a corrosive weapon, place one brilliant earth essence and any weapon into the Enchanter's Satchel, then cast <i>Melf's acid arrow</i> on the satchel.

Essences are automatically distilled from the remains of many creatures, such as elementals and most beasts. Such essences are typically only of volatile quality and ten must be combined using a Shaper's Alembic to create a brilliant variety.

Rarer recipes and essences might be discovered throughout your adventures.
207375 := This powerful alembic allows you to convert, combine, and divide essences. Essences are used to enchant items. They are automatically distilled from the remains of many creatures, such as elementals and most beasts. Typically, only volatile essences are found and the alembic must be used to convert them into brilliant essences for enchanting purposes. Items are enchanted by placing them in the Enchanter's Satchel along with an item, and then casting the appropriate spell. Many standard recipes are explained in the item description for any brilliant essence.

The abilities of the Shaper's Alembic include:
1. Combine Essences. Using this ability on a stack of lesser essences converts them into a more powerful one. No value is lost.
2. Divide Essence. Using this ability on a powerful essence converts it into an equivalent number of lesser essences. No value is lost.
3. Convert Essence. When used on a stack of elemental essences (fire, air, earth, water), two are converted into a single power essence of the same quality. When used on a power essence, several lesser essences are created of each elemental type.

Level: Druid 6, Wizard / Sorcerer 6

"So spoke Immith Yabog...

"In my youth, the spirit-eater curse was said to be rampant in the woodlands of the north. I was sent from Urling, with three of my hathran sisters, to seek the truth of these rumors.

"Outside the great forest, we came upon a fleeing mass of simple folk, who spoke fearfully of a foul cult - men and women who had begun to worship the spirit-eater as a god, who passed its power amongst themselves, and went into the deep forest to feed. 

"Retracing the villagers' steps, we soon came upon the encampment of these wicked folk, taking them by surprise, and slaying many. Only four managed to escape us, fleeing into the deep forest. One of these bore the dark hunger of a spirit-eater, and she devoured two of my sisters before she made her escape. My remaining sister and I dared not follow.

208633 := Spirit-eater
208634 := You have lost control of the hunger for spirits that has recently manifested inside of you. Your body now requires a periodic influx of energy obtained through the consumption of spirits, or it will eventually wither and die.

The vertical green bar represents your present level of spirit energy. It will drop over time (except during conversation), and as it falls, you will weaken at an accelerating rate. Each of the watermarks on the bar denotes a point at which your curse worsens to a new stage of debilitation. There are six stages of this affliction, the final of which is death. You may mouse over the watermark icons at any time to see what effects a particular stage of the affliction carries.

Several new abilities are available to you that will provide a means to replenish your spirit energy. They are available on the feats tab under "history."

The horizontal bar below the spirit energy bar is a measurement of your craving for spirits. The more you crave spirits, the faster your spirit energy is used up. Giving in to your urge to devour spirits more than once per day will tend to make you crave them more, while actively fighting to gain control over your hunger through the Suppress ability will ease that craving. Use extreme caution when deciding whether to devour spirits if you have already done so once that day - what may seem like a safe move to keep your health high could quite quickly lead you down a slippery slope where you are in constant need of spirits to devour just to stay alive.

Further details about spirit-eater abilities are available in their feat descriptions.

210373 := These scrolls appear to have been written by Myrkulite priests, centuries ago. They record the fates of many who opposed the former god of the dead, and they were probably read aloud to encourage fear of Myrkul and his faithful. At one time, there must have been many of these scrolls, but this one has decayed considerably, and much of it is missing. 
A prominent passage records the fate of a traitorous high priest:

"Know that all who follow the Lord of Bones shall face tests of faith. Not even his most favored are spared, as we are taught by the tale of Akachi the Betrayer.

"As a child, Akachi was offered as a Sacrifice to the church. Along with his brother, he was left unnamed upon our temple threshold, as was the custom in that time. Akachi was thus favored by our god, and named in the tradition of the eastern church, as are all those who come as babes into the faith of the dead. Indeed, he showed an uncanny faith as a boy - no poison or disease would touch him, and when the Black Whisper ravaged Mulsantir, he alone walked amongst the sick, hauled their corpses, and dug their graves unharmed. He offered salvation to those who would embrace the Lord of Bones, and it is said that those who converted to Myrkul's faith were healed.

"Each night, Akachi would return to the temple and entreat his fellow priests to join him in ministering to the dying, but all refused, except for Akachi's brother, Ereshi.  They remained hiding in the temple, fearful of the plague. So Myrkul permitted the Whisper to enter his church, carried upon the robes of the two young brothers, and all his cowering priests died coughing and rasping in their beds. Only Akachi and Ereshi survived, and the boy Akachi was annointed high priest of the Mulsantir temple.

"When the plague had passed, hundreds converted to Myrkul's faith, inspired by Akachi's courage and divine favor. While Ereshi ministered to the faithful, Akachi walked the surrounding lands and converted hundreds more souls to the Lord of Bones. Myrkul's eye was upon him, and our god would visit Akachi in his dreams, instructing him in the highest mysteries of the faith, and entrusting him with missions to destroy his enemies.

"Akachi became the hand of Myrkul's justice, hunting the foes of our god across the planes. No slight against the Lord of Bones went unpunished, no betrayal went unavenged... and no honor was denied Akachi, in return. In his hand he bore a silver blade, taken from the depths of the Hells at Myrkul's bidding, and granted to him as reward. Akachi was Chosen of Myrkul, favored above all.

"But with such favor come the greatest tests. Akachi's lover was a wizardess who cared little for the gods. One day, her enchantments went awry, and she was killed in a magical conflagration. Then was Akachi distraught, for he knew what awaited his beloved. All those who died without faith were bound into the Wall of the Faithless, and finally dissolved into the substance of the Wall. 

"Akachi entreated Myrkul to spare his lover. For this, he would pay any price, perform any service Myrkul might desire. But Myrkul's judgment is swift and sure, and it does not waver for those who deny the gods. Akachi's lover would remain in the Wall.

"In that moment, Akachi's pride outshone his faith. His anger turned to wrath, and he swore that he would tear down the Wall itself to take his lover back. And by this sinful vow, he was doomed, and he became the Betrayer.

"Akachi spoke wicked lies to his brother Ereshi, and turned him against Myrkul. By his devotion to his brother, Ereshi was also doomed. Ereshi set aside his name, and he took a new name that was given to him by his brother, as a token of his own betrayal. 

"And Akachi spoke lies to others as well, turning many faithful against the Lord of Bones. He opened the prison of Myrkul's vault and called forth the demilich Rammaq, who had thrice attempted to become a god, and had been thwarted by Akachi himself. The Betrayer made pacts with many others, as well, promising them great rewards when the Wall of the Faithless was overthrown. Among these were Zoab, a prince of Celestia, and Sey'ryu, a queen of dragonkind. When he had assembled a mighty host, Akachi carved a doorway between the Plane of Shadow and the realm of the dead, and he led his army into Myrkul's realm.

"In that hour, Myrkul appeared in his glory, at the head of an even greater host - all the heroes of the ancient dead marched at his back, with all the masses of the False, and many baatezu who had been summoned from the Hells. Akachi's army crumbled before the Lord of Bones, and his generals fled to the darkest corners of the planes. Not even the Betrayer could stand against Myrkul, in the realm of the dead. Akachi was dragged in chains to the Basilica of Lost Hope, and Myrkul pronounced Judgment upon him. 

"Be watchful, oh faithful of the Lord of Bones. For it is said that Akachi's generals still live, and that they promised to return, should the Betrayer ever stand before death's gates again. And it is also whispered that Akachi tore the soul of his lover from the Wall, before Myrkul struck him down. If this sacrilege is true, then she shall be hunted, and find no rest in this world... for the Faithless must be held to account, and none may challenge the judgment of the Lord of Bones."

210596 := The Story So Far
210597 := You were raised in the marsh village of West Harbor, on the Sword Coast. Your early years were uneventful - raised by your foster father, Daeghun, you grew to adulthood with little knowledge of your past. 

That changed just a few months ago, on the night of the High Harvest Festival. West Harbor was attacked by a force of githyanki - interplanar warriors who were seeking the lost shards of an ancient blade. You helped to repel their attack and save your village... only to be sent away by your foster father, bearing one of the mysterious shards to the city of Neverwinter. Along the way, you assembled a band of companions - some more loyal than others - that included Khelgar Ironfist, a hotheaded dwarf, Neeshka, a tiefling rogue, Casavir the paladin, Bishop the traitorous ranger, and others.

In Neverwinter, you discovered that the githyanki were only a small part of a much greater tale. The shards they sought were once a part of the legendary Sword of Gith, which had been shattered years ago, when the warlock Ammon Jerro wielded it against the monstrous King of Shadows. Their battle was fought in your village of West Harbor, when you were a mere infant... and as the Sword burst into dozens of shards, one of them struck you, and embedded itself near your heart.

You defeated the githyanki who pursued you, only to become embroiled in a new struggle against the King of Shadows, whose gathering armies now threatened Neverwinter and the Sword Coast. Over the course of your adventures, you earned a knighthood and were granted command of a castle, becoming Knight-Captain of Crossroad Keep. You also witnessed the destruction of your home village, which was razed by a servant of the King of Shadows... only your foster father and a few others survived.

In the end, you allied with the warlock Ammon Jerro and commanded the defenses of Crossroad Keep against an army of undead. Then you fought your way into the fortress of the King of Shadows and struck him down. But with the King's death, his fortress began to collapse... and you were unable to escape. You remember great blocks of stone tumbling around you... the cries of your surviving companions... then darkness, and nothing more.

210737 := These scrolls appear to have been written by Myrkulite priests, centuries ago. They record the fates of many who opposed the former god of the dead, and they were probably read aloud to encourage fear of Myrkul and his faithful. At one time, there must have been many of these scrolls, but this one has decayed considerably, and much of it is missing. 
A prominent passage records the fate of a traitorous high priest:

"Know that all who follow the Lord of Bones shall face tests of faith. Not even his most favored are spared, as we are taught by the tale of Akachi the Betrayer.

"As a child, Akachi was offered as a Sacrifice to the church. Along with his brother, he was left unnamed upon our temple threshold, as was the custom in that time. Akachi was thus favored by our god, and named in the tradition of the eastern church, as are all those who come as babes into the faith of the dead. Indeed, he showed an uncanny faith as a boy - no poison or disease would touch him, and when the Black Whisper ravaged Mulsantir, he alone walked amongst the sick, hauled their corpses, and dug their graves unharmed. He offered salvation to those who would embrace the Lord of Bones, and it is said that those who converted to Myrkul's faith were healed.

"Each night, Akachi would return to the temple and entreat his fellow priests to join him in ministering to the dying, but all refused, except for Akachi's brother, Eveshi.  They remained hiding in the temple, fearful of the plague. So Myrkul permitted the Whisper to enter his church, carried upon the robes of the two young brothers, and all his cowering priests died coughing and rasping in their beds. Only Akachi and Eveshi survived, and the boy Akachi was annointed high priest of the Mulsantir temple.

"When the plague had passed, hundreds converted to Myrkul's faith, inspired by Akachi's courage and divine favor. While Eveshi ministered to the faithful, Akachi walked the surrounding lands and converted hundreds more souls to the Lord of Bones. Myrkul's eye was upon him, and our god would visit Akachi in his dreams, instructing him in the highest mysteries of the faith, and entrusting him with missions to destroy his enemies.

"Akachi became the hand of Myrkul's justice, hunting the foes of our god across the planes. No slight against the Lord of Bones went unpunished, no betrayal went unavenged... and no honor was denied Akachi, in return. In his hand he bore a silver blade, taken from the depths of the Hells at Myrkul's bidding, and granted to him as reward. Akachi was Chosen of Myrkul, favored above all.

"But with such favor come the greatest tests. Akachi's lover was a wizardess who cared little for the gods. One day, her enchantments went awry, and she was killed in a magical conflagration. Then was Akachi distraught, for he knew what awaited his beloved. All those who died without faith were bound into the Wall of the Faithless, and finally dissolved into the substance of the Wall. 

"Akachi entreated Myrkul to spare his lover. For this, he would pay any price, perform any service Myrkul might desire. But Myrkul's judgment is swift and sure, and it does not waver for those who deny the gods. Akachi's lover would remain in the Wall.

"In that moment, Akachi's pride outshone his faith. His anger turned to wrath, and he swore that he would tear down the Wall itself to take his lover back. And by this sinful vow, he was doomed, and he became the Betrayer.

"Akachi spoke wicked lies to his brother Eveshi, and turned him against Myrkul. By his devotion to his brother, Eveshi was also doomed. Eveshi set aside his name, and he took a new name that was given to him by his brother, as a token of his own betrayal. 

"And Akachi spoke lies to others as well, turning many faithful against the Lord of Bones. He opened the prison of Myrkul's vault and called forth the demilich Rammaq, who had thrice attempted to become a god, and had been thwarted by Akachi himself. The Betrayer made pacts with many others, as well, promising them great rewards when the Wall of the Faithless was overthrown. Among these were Zoab, a prince of Celestia, and Sey'ryu, a queen of dragonkind. When he had assembled a mighty host, Akachi carved a doorway between the Plane of Shadow and the realm of the dead, and he led his army into Myrkul's realm.

"In that hour, Myrkul appeared in his glory, at the head of an even greater host - all the heroes of the ancient dead marched at his back, with all the masses of the False, and many baatezu who had been summoned from the Hells. Akachi's army crumbled before the Lord of Bones, and his generals fled to the darkest corners of the planes. Not even the Betrayer could stand against Myrkul, in the realm of the dead. Akachi was dragged in chains to the Basilica of Lost Hope, and Myrkul pronounced Judgment upon him. 

"Be watchful, oh faithful of the Lord of Bones. For it is said that Akachi's generals still live, and that they promised to return, should the Betrayer ever stand before death's gates again. And it is also whispered that Akachi tore the soul of his lover from the Wall, before Myrkul struck him down. If this sacrilege is true, then she shall be hunted, and find no rest in this world... for the Faithless must be held to account, and none may challenge the judgment of the Lord of Bones."

"So spoke Immith Yabog...

"In my youth, the spirit-eater curse was said to be rampant in the woodlands of the north. I was sent from Urling, with three of my hathran sisters, to seek the truth of these rumors.

"Outside the great forest, we came upon a fleeing mass of simple folk, who spoke fearfully of a foul cult - men and women who had begun to worship the spirit-eater as a god, who passed its power amongst themselves, and went into the deep forest to feed. 

"Retracing the villagers' steps, we soon came upon the encampment of these wicked folk, taking them by surprise, and slaying many. Only four managed to escape us, fleeing into the deep forest. One of these bore the dark hunger of a spirit-eater, and she devoured two of my sisters before she made her escape. My remaining sister and I dared not follow.

"But we learned much from the remains of their camp. These folk were unlike others afflicted by the curse - indeed, they referred to their dark hunger as the Gift. And we discovered that many of those we had taken for Rashemi were shapeshifted uthraki. The uthraki worshipped the one who possessed the Gift, and had learned much lore of the spirit-eater, to pass on to others who bore the hunger and reveled in it as they did..."

210848 := This small bag can be used to enchant items and functions like a portable workbench.

To enchant an item, simply place it in this satchel along with one or more brilliant <i>essences</i>, then cast the appropriate spell as indicated in the essence's description. For example, to create a frost weapon, place one brilliant water essence and any weapon into the Enchanter's Satchel, then cast <i>ice storm</i> on the satchel.

Essences are automatically distilled from the remains of many creatures, such as elementals and most beasts. Such essences are typically only of volatile quality and then must be combined using a Shaper's Alembic to create a brilliant variety.

Rarer recipes and essences might be discovered throughout your adventures.

This spell allows you to scribe a potent rune of power upon a surface. When triggered, a symbol of death slays one or more creatures within 60 feet of the symbol (treat as a burst) whose combined total current hit points do not exceed 150. The symbol of death affects the closest creatures first, skipping creatures with too many hit points to affect. The symbol lasts for 1 minute per caster level or until it has affected 150 hit points' worth of creatures, whichever comes first. Any creature that enters the area while the symbol of death is active is subject to its effect, whether or not that creature was in the area when it was triggered.  A symbol of death is triggered whenever a creature touches the rune or passes over the rune. You and all creatures within your party are automatically attuned to the rune and as such cannot trigger it and are immune to its effects, even if within its radius when triggered. 

Note: Magic traps such as symbol of death are hard to detect and disable. A rogue (only) can use the Search skill to find a symbol of death and Disable Device to thwart it. The DC in each case is 25 + spell level, or 33 for symbol of death. Also, a symbol of death can be removed by a successful dispel magic targeted on the rune.

211138 := <color=Gold><b>Swashbuckler</b></color>

The swashbuckler embodies the concepts of daring and panache. Favoring agility and wit over brute force, the swashbuckler excels both in combat situations and social interactions, making her a versatile character indeed.

<color=Gold>Class Features:</color>

- <b>Hit Die:</b> d10

- <b>Base Attack Bonus:</b> High.

- <b>High Saves:</b> Fortitude.

- <b>Weapon Proficiencies:</b> Simple and martial weapons.

- <b>Armor Proficiencies:</b>  Light armor.

- <b>Skill Points:</b> 4 + Int modifier per level, x4 at first level.

- <b>Class Skills:</b> Bluff, Craft Armor, Craft Weapon, Diplomacy, Lore, Parry, Taunt, and Tumble.

- <b>Weapon Finesse:</b> A swashbuckler gains Weapon Finesse as a bonus feat at 1st level even if she does not qualify for the feat.

- <b>Grace:</b> A swashbuckler gains a +1 bonus on Reflex saves at 2nd level. This bonus increases to +2 at 11th level, to +3 at 20th level, and to +4 at 29th level.  A swashbuckler loses this bonus when wearing medium or heavy armor or when encumbered.

- <b>Insightful Strike:</b> At 3rd level, a swashbuckler becomes able to place her finesse attacks where they deal greater damage.  She applies her Intelligence bonus (if any) as a bonus on damage rolls (in addition to any Strength bonus she may have) with any light weapon, as well as any other weapon that can be used with Weapon Finesse, such as a rapier.  Targets immune to sneak attacks or critical hits are immune to the swashbuckler's insightful strike.  A swashbuckler cannot use this ability when wearing medium or heavy armor or when encumbered.

- <b>Swashbuckler Dodge:</b> A swashbuckler is trained at focusing her defense on a single opponent in melee.  She gains a +1 dodge bonus to AC against melee attacks from her current target or last attacker.  This bonus increases by +1 at every five levels after 5th (+2 at 10th level, +3 at 15th, +4 at 20th, +5 at 25th, and +6 at 30th).  A swashbuckler loses this bonus when wearing medium or heavy armor or when encumbered.

- <b>Mobility:</b> At 7th level, a swashbuckler gains Mobility as a bonus feat even if she does not qualify for it.

- <b>Improved Flanking:</b> A swashbuckler of 8th level or higher who is flanking an opponent gains a +4 bonus on attacks instead of a +2 bonus on attacks.

- <b>Lucky:</b> At 11th level, a swashbuckler gains Luck of Heroes as a bonus feat.

- <b>Acrobatic Skill Mastery:</b> At 13th level, a swashbuckler becomes so certain in the use of her acrobatic skills that she can use them reliably even under adverse conditions.  When making a Tumble check, a swashbuckler cannot roll less than 5, even if in combat. 

- <b>Weakening Critical:</b> A swashbuckler of 14th level or higher who scores a critical hit against a creature also deals 2 points of Strength damage to the creature.  Creatures immune to critical hits are immune to this effect.

- <b>Slippery Mind:</b> When a swashbuckler reaches 17th level, her mind becomes more difficult to control. If the swashbuckler fails her save against an enchantment spell or effect, she automatically gets one reroll. She gets only this one extra chance to succeed at a certain saving throw.

-<b>Wounding Critical:</b>  A swashbuckler of 19th level or higher who scores a critical hit against a creature also deals 2 points of Constitution damage to the creature.  (This damage is in addition to the Strength damage dealt by the swashbuckler's weakening critical class feature.) Creatures immune to critical hits are immune to this effect.

Use: Automatic, though a condition that negates a Dexterity bonus to AC also negates any dodge bonuses. Multiple dodge bonuses (different feats, racial bonuses) are cumulative.

211240 := <color=Gold><b>Doomguide</b></color>

<color=Red>(PRESTIGE CLASS: This class is not available at character creation and must be unlocked by meeting special requirements, listed below.)</color>

Those who worry about life after death turn to the doomguides of Kelemvor, an elite order of spellcasting warriors in service to the Judge of the Damned, to answer their fears with promises of a painless transition and a fair judgement in the afterlife. When not administering to the needs of those about to die, doomguides halt the spread of necromancy by cleansing the taint of unlife through careful application of faith, spells, and bladecraft. As both compassionate undertakers and vigorous foes of undead, doomguides represent the inherent dualism that defines death in the Realms. Doomguides come exclusively from the ranks of Kelemvor's clergy.

<color=Gold>Requirements:</color>

<b>Alignment:</b> Any Lawful.

<b>Skills:</b> Diplomacy 5 ranks

<b>Feats:</b> Extra Turning, Great Fortitude

<b>Spells:</b> Level 3 divine spellcaster

<b>Deity:</b> Kelemvor

<color=Gold>Class Features:</color>

- <b>Hit Die:</b> d6

- <b>Base Attack Bonus:</b> High.

- <b>High Saves:</b> Will.

- <b>Weapon Proficiencies:</b> Doomguides gain no weapon proficiencies.

- <b>Armor Proficiencies:</b> Doomguides gain no armor proficiencies.

- <b>Skill Points:</b> 2 + Int Modifier.

- <b>Class Skills:</b> Concentration, Craft Alchemy, Craft Armor, Craft Weapon, Diplomacy, Heal, Lore, and Spellcraft

- <b>Spells Per Day:</b> At each doomguide level, the character gains new spells per day as if he had also gained a level in a divine spellcasting class to which he belonged before adding the prestige class level. He does not, however, gain any other benefit a character of that class would have gained.

- <b>Kelemvor's Boon:</b> By the grace of the Lord of the Dead, doomguides add their doomguide class levels to their cleric levels for purposes turning or destroying undead, both for the initial turning check and the turning damage roll.

- <b>Bonus Feats:</b> Bonus Feats: At Level 2, the Doomguide gains Improved Turning. At level 3, they gain Extra Turning II. At level 6, they gain Divine Vengeance. At level 10, they gain Empower Turning and Extra Turning III.

- <b>Save Bonus:</b> At 4th level, doomguides get a +4 bonus on saving throws against death effects and to saving throws to overcome a negative level. Upon reaching 8th level, a doomguide always makes his saving throw to overcome a negative level.

- <b>Bond of <i>Fatal Touch</i> :</b> The doomguide's devotion to Kelemvor and dedication to the teachings of the Lord of the Crystal Spire has helped him to establish certain supernatural links to <i>Fatal Touch</i>, Kelemvor's powerful bastard sword. These links manifest in the form of a pale green nimbus around the weapon, representing the ability of a doomguide to increase the power of the weapons he wields.

The ability lasts for 1 round each time it is used, and can be invoked  a number of times per day equal to the doomguide's Charisma bonus (minimum one). A doomguide must decide to use the ability before attacking, and if the attack misses that use is wasted.

At 5th level, the bond grants wielded weapons the <i>ghost touch</i> property. At 7th level, weapons wielded by the doomguide gain both <i>ghost touch</i> and the <i>undead bane</i> properties. At 9th level, wielded weapons gain the <i>ghost touch, undead bane</i>, and <i>disruption</i> properties even if they are not bludgeoning weapons. The weapon's normal abilities still apply.

- <b>Ethereal Purge:</b> At 8th level, once per day the doomguide may surround himself with a sphere of power with a radius of 5 feet per class level that forces all concealed creatures in the area to manifest on or shift themselves to the Material Plane, as appropriate. Such creatures may attempt a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 doomguide's class level + doomguide's Wisdom bonus) to resist this effect. Those who fail suffer the above effects and are prevented from returning to concealment for 1 minute per class level.

- <b>Kelemvor's Grace:</b> At 10th level, a doomguide gains complete immunity to death effects. Furthermore, allies within 10 feet of him gain a +4 bonus on saving throws against death effects and to saving throws to overcome a negative level.

214452 := Torrid Spear of Rejuvenation
214453 := This spear once belonged to Turoc, the spirit shaman of an ogre clan whose name has long since been forgotten. His spear - battle hardened by the myriad of conflicts Turoc had been involved in defending the clan's territory - would also look renewed, as if a new spear had been fashioned. It wasn't until the shaman's apprentice followed his master into the mountains that someone found out what the truth really was.

The young ogre's name was Kithrak, and he had been Turoc's apprentice for several years before he finally found the courage to follow his master's footsteps into the mountains. Once the old shaman arrived at his destination, for three days and nights he was enveloped in a divine light. A voice, booming presumably from the Heavens themselves, would speak to the ogre, but in a language Kithrak did not comprehend. Fearing that Turoc would no longer have him as his apprentice, the young ogre stayed his tongue, never telling anyone of what he had witnessed.

Many years later, the old shaman, weary of the endless fights his clan would wage, asked his apprentice to join him in his pilgrimage. It is thought that Turoc wanted to pass his knowledge and power to Kithrak, that he was no longer willing to carry the burden. No one knows for sure, as the two never returned. Shortly thereafter, the clan itself disappeared... not a trace of any of them remained. Tales told among the ogre clans say that the apprentice was not ready to wield the divine power held by his master. Others say that the apprentice tried to murder his master, and he and his clan were destroyed by the gods as punishment. Whatever the truth may be, all that remains as proof of the clan's existence is this spear.

220738 := Bond of Fatal Touch
220740 := Type of Feat: Class.
Prerequisite: Doomguide Level 5.
Specifics: The doomguide's devotion to Kelemvor and dedication to the teachings of the Lord of the Crystal Spire has helped him to establish a certain supernatural links to Fatal Touch, Kelemvor's powerful scythe. These links manifest in the form of a pale green nimbus around a weapon, representing the ability of the doomguide to increase the power of the weapon he wields. The ability lasts for 1 attack each time it is used and can be invoked a number of times per day equal to the doomguide's charisma bonus (minimum 1). A doomguide must decide to use the ability before attacking and if the attack misses that use is wasted. 

At 5th level the bond grants wielded weapons a damage bonus against undead. At 7th level weapons gain both the damage bonus and <i>undead bane</i> properties. At 9th level wielded weapons gain the damage bonus, <i>undead bane</i> and <i>disruption</i> properties even if they are not bludgeoning weapons. The weapons normal abilities still applies.

<color=Gold><b>Weapon Traits:</b></color>

- <b>Damage Bonus:</b> The Doomguide's devotion to Kelemvor grants wielded weapons a damage bonus of 1d6 against undead foes.

- <b>Undead Bane:</b> A bane weapon excels at attacking one type or subtype of creature. Against its designated foe, its effective enhancement bonus is +2 better than its normal enhancement bonus. It deals an extra 2d6 points of damage against the foe.

- <b>Disruption:</b> A weapon of disruption is the bane of all undead. Any undead creature struck in combat must succeed on a DC 14 Will save or be destroyed.

Use: Selected.

220754 := hellfire warlock
220755 := <color=Gold><b>Hellfire Warlock</b></color>

<color=Red>(PRESTIGE CLASS: This class is not available at character creation and must be unlocked by meeting special requirements, listed below.)</color>

The hellfire warlocks are a secretive group of specialist warlocks who have mastered hellfire, a dangerous energy found only in the Nine Hells. By tapping into this infernal power, these characters learn to infuse their eldritch blasts with the dark power of hellfire.

<color=Gold>Requirements:</color>

<b>Skills:</b> Intimidate 6 ranks, Spellcraft 6 ranks, Lore 12 ranks.

<b>Spells:</b> Brimstone Blast or Hellrime Blast

<color=Gold>Class Features:</color>

- <b>Hit Die:</b> d6

- <b>Base Attack Bonus:</b> Medium.

- <b>High Saves:</b> Will.

- <b>Weapon Proficiencies:</b> Simple weapons.

- <b>Armor Proficiencies:</b> Light armor.  A warlock can use any of his invocations while wearing light armor without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. A warlock wearing medium or heavy armor or using a shield incurs a chance of arcane spell failure.

- <b>Skill Points:</b> 2 + Int Modifier.

- <b>Class Skills:</b> Concentration, Intimidate, Lore,  Spellcraft, Use Magic Device.

- <b>Hellfire Blast:</b> Whenever you use your eldritch blast ability, you can change your eldritch blast into a hellfire blast. A hellfire blast deals your normal eldritch blast damage plus an extra 2d6 points of damage per class level. If your blast hits multiple targets (for example, the eldritch chain or eldritch cone blast shape invocations), each target takes the extra damage. This damage is not fire damage. The Hellfire Warlock takes 1 point of Constitution damage each target hit in this manner.

- <b>Invoking:</b> At each level, you gain new invocations known, increased damage with eldritch blast, and an increase in invoker level as if you had also gained a level in the warlock class. You do not, however, gain any other benefit a character of that class would have gained.

- <b>Resistance to Fire 10:</b> At 2nd level, you gain resistance to fire 10. This resistance stacks with any resistance to fire you have gained from warlock class levels.

- <b>Summon Baatezu:</b> At 2nd level, once per day, the Hellfire Warlock can randomly summon a powerful devil from the Nine Hells to fight for the party. Control of the Baatezu lasts for a number of rounds equal to 1D8 + the Hellfire Warlock's class level + their Charisma bonus.  When the ability expires, the caster loses dominance over the Baatezu - which can have disastrous consequences, as devils typically despise being bothered by lesser beings. The caster is advised not to leave this up to chance, and dispel this summons before this time is up, sending the Baatezu back to the Nine Hells - though the devil might not attack, this method is the <i>only</i> certain way of avoiding a violent confrontation with the angry creature. 

- <b>Hellfire Shield:</b>  Starting at 3rd level, you can call up hellfire to surround yourself with a protective barrier.  This barrier deals damage equal to your eldritch blast (including bonus damage from the hellfire blast ability). This barrier automatically strikes the target every round, which can attempt a Reflex saving throw for half damage (DC 10 + 1/2 your character level + your Cha modifier). Each time this ability hits an enemy creature, you take 1 point of Constitution damage. Because the diabolical forces behind the power of hellfire demand part of your essence in exchange for this granted power, if you do not have a Constitution score or are somehow immune to Constitution damage, you cannot use this ability.

220779 := Hellfire Shield
220780 := Type of Feat: Class
Prerequisites: Hellfire Warlock Level 3.
Specifics: Starting at 3rd level, you can call up hellfire to surround yourself with a protective barrier.  This barrier deals damage equal to your eldritch blast (including bonus damage from the hellfire blast ability). This barrier automatically strikes the target every round, which can attempt a Reflex saving throw for half damage (DC 10 + 1/2 your character level + your Cha modifier). Each time this ability hits an enemy creature, you take 1 point of Constitution damage. Because the diabolical forces behind the power of hellfire demand part of your essence in exchange for this granted power, if you do not have a Constitution score or are somehow immune to Constitution damage, you cannot use this ability.
Use: Combat mode.

220823 := <color=Gold><b>Yuan-ti Pureblood</b></color>

The yuan-ti are descended from humans whose bloodlines have been mingled with those of snakes. Their evilness, cunning, and ruthlessness are legendary. Yuan-ti constantly scheme to advance their own dark agendas. They are calculating and suave enough to form alliances with other evil creatures when necessary, but they always put their own interests first.

Yuan-ti that can pass for humans with suitable clothing, cosmetics, and magic are known as Purebloods. These creatures are usually charged with infiltrating humanoid societies and managing covert operations that require direct contact with humanoids.

<color=Gold><b>Racial Traits:</b></color>

- <b>Ability Adjustments:</b> +2 Dexterity, +2 Intelligence, +2 Charisma
 
- <b>Darkvision:</b> Yuan-ti purebloods can see in the dark up to 60 feet.

- <b>Scaled Skin:</b> +1 Natural Armor Bonus.

- <b>Spell Resistant:</b> Spell resistance of 11+ character level.

- <b>Snake Senses:</b> You gain the feats Alertness (+2 to Spot and Listen skills) and Blind-Fight (bonuses to fighting while blind or against invisible creatures) for free.

- <b>Spell-Like Abilities (1/day): </b>
     <i>Animal Trance</i>
     <i>Cause Fear</i>
     <i>Charm Person</i>
     <i>Darkness</i>
     <i>Entangle</i>

- <b>Level adjustment:</b> +2

- <b>Favored Class:</b> Ranger

225133 := Gray Orc
225134 := Gray Orcs
225135 := gray orc
225136 := gray orcs
225137 := <color=Gold><b>Gray Orc</b></color=Gold>

The orcs of the eastern lands are concentrated in the Moonsea and Endless Wastes today, with a much smaller number scattered through the various lands that lie between. A gray orc looks less bestial than their more savage northern kin, but is still obviously nonhuman. Grey orcs are more apt to wear "civilized" clothing than mountain orcs, though they typically follow a nomadic existence - dwelling in remote, desolate places and eking out a meager existence as best they can. The true power behind a tribe of gray orcs is not the chieftain, but the tribe's high priest, typically an adept or a cleric (often female), who has held the position for many years. The gray orcs are zealots, and the word of their tribal clerics is law.

Gray orcs are just as mean, savage, and barbaric as their northern cousins, but they lack the mountain orc's drive to conquer and enslave. Gray orcs are quite likely to react suddenly and irrationally to events, trusting their heart and instincts more readily than logic. When presented with an opportunity to attack a hated rival, a gray orc doesn't hesitate to attack even having been brutally defeated dozens of times before by the same enemy.

<color=Gold><b>Racial Traits:</b></color>

- <b>Ability Adjustments:</b> +2 Strength, -2 Intelligence, +2 Wisdom, -2 Charisma

- <b>Long Gait:</b> Gray orc base land speed is 40 feet. Their gait is long and loping and they can cover great distances quickly.

- <b>Light Sensitivity:</b> Gray orcs suffer a -1 penalty on attack rolls in sunlight or within the radius of a <i>daylight</i> spell.

- <b>Scent:</b> Can detect approaching enemies, sniff out hidden foes, and track by sense of smell. This allows the user to track hidden and invisible targets when using the Track ability.

- <b> Favored Class:</b> Cleric. Although gray orcs are comfortable with the savage life of the barbarian, they tend to be more calm and collected than northern orcs, focusing their rage and hatred inward. This allows them to excel as clerics of the warlike orc deities.

- <b>Level Adjustment +1:</b> Gray orcs are slightly more powerful and gain levels more slowly than other, more common races. It will take more experience for a gray orc to reach level 2 than it would for normal races, for example.

Gray orcs are marginally cleaner than mountain orcs, and their equipment is kept in better shape as a result - axes in particular are viewed as holy, and gray orcs take fastidious care of their greataxe.

231910 := Cadorna Family Sword
231911 := Created to commemorate the fiftieth anniversary of Magnus Cadorna's unlikely victory against a young red dragon, the Cadorna Family Sword was passed down through four generations until it left the family's possession.

Originally a small family of weavers from the Dragon Reach, the Cadorna family fell on hard times when a dragon began plaguing the region near their village.  The oldest son of the family, Magnus, joined a local militia in a weak attempt to control the dragon's ransacking.

When adventurers finally arrived to deal with the dragon, the militia waited in reserve in case the adventurers failed.  The adventurers did fail, and the wounded dragon set out to take vengeance against the villagers who had helped his would-be killers.

In a short but bloody battle, most of the militiamen were killed. Desperate and half dead, Magnus Cadorna dove at the wounded creature and struck a fatal blow. The hero of the village, Magnus received treasure and honors that elevated the family to a prominent position. They soon spread out across the Dragon Reach as a powerful textile trading company.

When Magnus was eighty two years old, the Cadorna Family Sword was created to commemorate the event that catapulted the family to prosperity. Magnus appreciated the gesture, but also found it a bit "silly". The sword was passed down for a few generations in the self-styled "dragon killer" family until it came into the possession of junior councilman Porphyrys Cadorna in the ill-fated city of Phlan.

Porphyrys was eventually run out of town for his complicity with enemies of the city. Though he lived for many years after the tragic events that lead to his family's shame and ruin, Porphyrys never found an heir to continue his line. He entrusted the family sword to his loyal servant and bodyguard, a tough soldier who called himself "Skullcrusher".

This cold iron blade was crafted with high attention to detail. Its extensive engravings are intricate and ornate, though some of the designs have been blemished by heavy use in battle. One side of the blade contains an illustration of a family history that begins with a weaver's loom and culiminates with a battle against a menacing dragon. The blade's other face contains a family tree for the Cadorna line. A more recent engraving can be found on the hilt, "To Skullcrusher, For All Your Service - P. Cadorna, 1351 DR".

233506 := Welcome to <i>Neverwinter Nights 2: Storm of Zehir</i>!

In <i>Storm of Zehir</i> we have introduced three distinct <b>Play Modes</b> - which you can use to make controlling your characters and camera easier. Each Play Mode features a different camera and control style, and you can customize the styles further to suit your own options. The Play Modes are designed to make it possible to quickly and easily to switch between these different camera and control styles based on the current gameplay situation.

The three modes are:

	<b>Exploration Mode</b> - This mode features a top-down camera that always remains focused on the currently controlled party member. By default, left-click and hold in this mode will cause the currently controlled character to walk in the direction of the mouse cursor. This mode is most useful when you want to be able to see your entire party and all of your surroundings, but want to keep the camera focused on one character.
	<b>Character Mode</b> - This mode features an over-the shoulder camera that remains focused on the currently controlled party member - and by default, will refocus directly behind that character whenever you begin moving. By default, you can left-click and hold and then move the mouse to turn your character. This mode is fantastic for getting a good look at your surroundings from the point of view of your character - and is also useful for a more immersive role-playing experience.
	<b>Strategy Mode</b> - This mode features a Top-Down camera that is not focused on the currently controlled character. You can move the mouse to any edge of the screen, or use the Keyboard (Default: Arrow Keys) to scroll the camera in this mode. There is a limit to the amount that the camera can scroll in this mode, based upon your selected options and the visual range of your party. Additionally, you can click and drag in this mode to select multiple characters. This mode is fantastic for controlling your party in difficult combat situations, or any time when you need to rapidly issue commands to your party.

The default mode for <i>Storm of Zehir</i> is <b>Exploration Mode</b>, however we encourage you to try out the different modes and find which you prefer - or to switch between them (Default: Numpad * ) depending upon the situation.

233930 := NX2 - Tavern, Sword Coast Vocal
233931 := Type of Feat: Item Creation
Prerequisite: Caster level 3rd.
Specifics: This feat grants the ability to craft a wide variety of magical items, including amulets ,rings, gloves, bracers, cloaks, belts, helms, and boots.
Using this feat to craft magical items requires several things: a magical workbench, a magic item recipe, and the ingredients/skills listed within the recipe. Each recipe is unique and possesses its own requirements, but any party members can supply these - including ingredients, caster level, or skill rank minimums.
Once all requirements for crafting the item are met, the player must be in close proximity to a magical workbench, and activate the recipe. If all the ingredients are present, the minimum skill ranks are met, and the crafting player is within 10 meters of a magician's workbench, the item will be crafted.
Crafting ingredients can vary widely - gems, creature parts, gold, gear, and trade goods can be included. Gear - such as travelling cloaks or leather boots - can be found at any merchant, while gems are carried in more exclusive stores. Creature parts can be found in the stores of bounty collectors, or dropped off the corpse of the creature in question. More exotic ingredients must be found through adventuring.
Many useful recipes can be purchased from merchants that sell magical wares. High powered magic recipes are not as commonplace - as many casters jealously guard their secrets. Anyone wishing to acquire such powerful recipes must search diligently throughout the world. 
Use: Selected.

233932 := Type of Feat: Item Creation
Prerequisite: Caster level 5th.
Specifics: This feat grants the ability to create magic weapons, armor, and shields.
Using this feat to craft magical arms or armor requires several things: a magical workbench, a magic weapon or armor recipe, and the ingredients/skills listed within the recipe. Each recipe is unique and possesses its own requirements, but any party members can supply these - including ingredients, caster level, or skill rank minimums.
Once all requirements for crafting the item are met, the player must be in close proximity to a magical workbench, activate the recipe, and apply the enchantment to the  weapon or armor of their choice. If all the ingredients are present, the minimum skill ranks are met, and the crafting player is within 10 meters of a magician's workbench, the item will be enchanted. <b>NOTE:</b> A magical  weapon, shield, or suit of armor can have a maximum of three enchantments on it.
Crafting ingredients can vary widely - gems, creature parts, gold, gear, and trade goods can be included. Gear - such as travelling cloaks or leather boots - can be found at any merchant, while gems are carried in more exclusive stores. Creature parts can be found in the stores of bounty collectors, or dropped off the corpse of the creature in question. More exotic ingredients must be found through adventuring.
Many useful recipes can be purchased from merchants that sell magical wares. High powered magic recipes are not as commonplace - as many casters jealously guard their secrets. Anyone wishing to acquire such powerful recipes must search diligently throughout the world. 
Use: Selected.

233933 := Ability: Intelligence
Requires Training: No.
Classes: All.
This skill is used to turn alchemical items into various trap kits. 
Creating a trap kit requires the appropriate recipe and ingredients. Most trap recipes include various alchemical items, hence the best trap makers are generally alchemists as well. More powerful traps require additional ranks in this skill. 
To create the trap, the player simply activates the recipe. Trap making recipes are often available for purchase in certain, less than reputable stores. 
Unlike other crafting professions, crafting traps does not require a workbench of any kind once the ingredients are collected. This makes crafting traps very versatile and accessible in dangerous locations. 
Use: Selected.

233948 := Animal Trance
Enchantment
Level: Brd 2, Drd 2
Components: V, S
Casting Time: Instant
Range: Close (25 ft. + 5 ft./2 levels)
Targets: Animals or magical beasts with Intelligence 1 or 2
Duration: 1 round per class level.
Saving Throw: No
Spell Resistance: Yes

Your swaying motions and music (or singing, or chanting) compel animals and magical beasts to do nothing but watch you for number of rounds equal to your class level. Only a creature with an Intelligence score of 1 or 2 can be fascinated by this spell. Roll 2d6 to determine the total number of HD worth of creatures that you fascinate. The closest targets are selected first until no more targets within range can be affected. For example, if Vadania affects 7 HD worth of animals and there are several 2 HD wolves within close range, only the three closest wolves are affected.
